issues.body: ProtocolAnnotations::admits returns true for MaliciousSecurity whenever no assertion contains SECX_SEMI_HONEST, and likewise for DishonestMajority. Thus an existing protocol entry with an empty assertions vector, an assertion with an empty assumption set, or assertions silently discarded by assertion_from_pairs because assurance is missing/unknown is admitted for both stronger threat models. admits_protocol only rejects a missing map key, so it does not provide the documented fail-closed behavior. The included hypothetical test even codifies absence of SemiHonest as positive evidence of malicious security, although the module says malicious/covert assumptions are unrepresentable. The separate drift guard does not protect callers because admits_protocol neither invokes it nor requires validated annotations.
issues.fix_hint: Represent positive support for each adversary requirement explicitly and admit only when that support is present and the annotation is structurally valid; absence of SemiHonest/HonestMajority must not imply a stronger guarantee. Alternatively return a validated annotation type from parsing and make admission possible only after validation that rejects empty/malformed assertions and unknown adversary axes. Add mutation tests for an empty block, missing/unknown assurance, and missing assumptions, asserting all requirements are denied. Update the current data-driven hypothetical test to include explicit malicious-security evidence once the vocabulary can represent it.
issues.title: Admission fails open when an annotation has no usable assumptions

verdict.summary: The annotation graph is appropriately opt-in and the shipped Turtle is candid about the semi-honest, externally unaudited posture. However, the public admission API is not actually fail-closed for malformed or incomplete annotations: it interprets absence of a limiting assumption as satisfaction of the stronger requirement. This is a security-significant mismatch with the documented invariant and must be corrected before approval.
